cards.explanation: The answer is life. The writer says sound judgment and discernment "…will be life to your soul and adornment to your neck." (Proverbs 3:22). Life for the soul AND something to wear around the neck. That's a two-for-one, friends, like a cookie that shows up with extra chocolate chips.

The answer is False. The writer says, "Then you will go on your way in safety, and your foot will not stumble." (Proverbs 3:23). It's tied to holding on to sound judgment and discernment. No stumbling, friends, and no small print about an exception.

The answer is that he won't be afraid. The writer says, "When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet." (Proverbs 3:24). He's telling his son to preserve sound judgment and discernment, and this promise is part of what follows. No fear when you lie down, and sweet sleep when you rest. I'd sign up for that one TWICE, friends.

The answer is that the LORD will be his confidence. The writer says, "…for the LORD will be your confidence and will keep your foot from the snare." (Proverbs 3:26). The reason isn't the son's eyesight or his muscles, friends. It's the LORD.

The answer is good. "Do not withhold good from the deserving when it is within your power to act." (Proverbs 3:27). If you can help, help. The verse hands you the moment the second you're able, friends. Don't sit on it like dough you forgot to bake.

The answer is False. The writer says not to tell your neighbor to come back tomorrow, and then adds, "…when you already have the means." (Proverbs 3:28). That last part is the key, friends. If it's in your hands, there's no reason to make them wait.

The answer is that he trusts you and lives beside you. The writer says, "Do not devise evil against your neighbor, for he trustfully dwells beside you." (Proverbs 3:29). Your neighbor feels safe right next door, friends. Plotting against someone like that is a terrible way to thank them.

The answer is cause. "Do not accuse a man without cause, when he has done you no harm." (Proverbs 3:30). No reason, no harm done, no accusing. Simple as that, friends. The writer keeps it short because it really is that clear.
The answer is envy him. "Do not envy a violent man or choose any of his ways…" (Proverbs 3:31). Two things on the list, friends: don't envy him, and don't pick up his ways. Both are off the shelf.

The answer is True. "…for the LORD detests the perverse, but He is a friend to the upright." (Proverbs 3:32). Read that second half again slowly, friends: a friend to the upright. That's a great thing for the LORD to be to someone.

The answer is the humble. "He mocks the mockers, but gives grace to the humble." (Proverbs 3:34). This verse is a pair, friends, and the two halves pull in opposite directions. Mockers get mocked, the humble get grace, and I know which side of that pair I'd rather stand on.

The answers are honor and shame. "The wise will inherit honor, but fools are held up to shame." (Proverbs 3:35). Honor is what the wise inherit, and shame is where fools are held up. This is the closing line of the passage, friends. Put the honor and the shame side by side and the pair is clear, folded up neat.
